text.en: On a winter night in 1914, enemy soldiers on a battlefield put down their guns to sing.

The text is a letter written on Christmas Day 1914 by a British soldier to his sister Janet. He tells her about Christmas Eve on the battlefields of France, when he sang carols with enemy soldiers. It seems almost like a fairy tale, and all enmity was forgotten as British and German soldiers celebrated Christmas together.
The truce shows that ordinary people on both sides longed for peace and that kindness can cross the lines of war.
Learn the words truce, dugout, trench, carol, enmity and replacements. Note the letter format: date, greeting My dear sister Janet and the closing.
